title: 14CO2-based assay for measuring Rubisco activity & activation state
author: Cristina Rodrigues Gabriel Sales
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bf8cjrsw
materials: Gold Star Quanta scintillation cocktail Room temperature, (storage)
SOLUTIONS TO PREPARE JUST BEFORE USE Prepared with reagents/solutions described in step 1.

START Thaw the frozen solutions that will be used in the day. Turn on the heat block and set to the temperature to be used for Rubisco activity measurements. The temperature to be used for the Rubisco activity measurement depends on the experiment goals. Typical measurement temperatures are 25 °C (standard) and 30 °C , depending on the species. Assays can be performed at a range of temperatures, however special care should be taken at high temperatures (e.g. 50 °C ), as this can lead to evaporation of the assay mix; rates will be faster, i.e. the assay might become less sensitive; and may cause difficulty in handling hot vials. Turn on the centrifuge and set to 4 °C . Collect samples from -80 °C into liquid nitrogen. Prepare the complete extraction buffer (step 2.1) and the complete assay buffer (step 2.2) and keep it On ice .

steps.title: Prepare basic extraction buffer (1x)
steps.instruction: Make a 1× basic extraction buffer containing 50 mM Bicine‑NaOH (pH 8.2), 20 mM MgCl₂·6H₂O, 1 mM EDTA, 2 mM Benzamidine, 5 mM ε‑Aminocaproic acid. Dissolve in ultrapure H₂O, adjust pH to 8.2 with NaOH, degas by bubbling N₂ for 5 min per 100 mL, then add 50 mM 2‑Mercaptoethanol. Aliquot (e.g., 50 mL Falcon tubes) and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Make 100 mM PMSF stock
steps.instruction: Dissolve PMSF to a final concentration of 100 mM in 99 % ethanol. Store the solution at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare basic assay buffer (2x)
steps.instruction: Prepare a 2× basic assay buffer containing 200 mM Bicine‑NaOH (pH 8.2) and 40 mM MgCl₂·6H₂O. Dissolve in ultrapure H₂O, adjust pH to 8.2 with NaOH, degas by bubbling N₂ for 5 min per 100 mL, aliquot, and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare 30 mM RuBP stock
steps.instruction: Dissolve RuBP to 30 mM in ultrapure H₂O. Store at –20 °C. Use high‑purity RuBP (≥99 %) to avoid inhibition by analogs.

steps.title: Label and store NaH¹⁴CO₃ solution
steps.instruction: Prepare 0.1 M NaH¹⁴CO₃ (specific activity 0.5 Ci mol⁻¹). Label clearly and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Make 1 M DTT stock
steps.instruction: Dissolve DTT to 1 M in ultrapure H₂O. Store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Assemble complete extraction buffer (1x)
steps.instruction: Combine the 1× basic extraction buffer (Step 1) with 10 mM DTT (from Step 6), 1 mM PMSF (from Step 2), and 1 % (v/v) plant protease‑inhibitor cocktail. Adjust the final volume to cover all extractions for the day plus two extra aliquots. Mix on ice. Volume depends on leaf mass and protein content; test beforehand to keep Rubisco concentration within assay sensitivity.

steps.title: Prepare complete assay buffer per vial
steps.instruction: For each 250 µL reaction, mix 2× basic assay buffer (Step 3) to give a final 1× concentration, 50 µL 100 mM NaH¹⁴CO₃ (Step 5) to give a final 10 mM concentration, and 165 µL ultrapure H₂O. Optionally add 2 mM KH₂PO₄ for field samples. Prepare enough volume for all duplicates, blanks, and a small excess (e.g., for 10 extractions calculate 43 vials).

steps.title: Set up assay vials
steps.instruction: Immediately before extraction, place four 1.5 mL vials in a heat block. Add 465 µL of the complete assay buffer (Step 8) to each vial. To the two vials designated for initial activity, add 10 µL of 30 mM RuBP (Step 4). Keep vials on the heat block until use.

steps.title: Extract Rubisco from leaf tissue
steps.instruction: Add the complete extraction buffer (Step 7) to an ice‑cold mortar. Transfer a frozen leaf sample (from liquid N₂) into the mortar and grind thoroughly for 30–60 s. Transfer the homogenate to an ice‑cold 1.5 mL microtube and centrifuge at 14 000 × g, 4 °C for 1 min. Keep all steps on ice; the whole extraction should not exceed 1 min. Transfer the supernatant to a new ice‑cold tube and proceed directly to the assay.

steps.title: Add extract to assay vials
steps.instruction: Add 25 µL of the leaf extract to each of the four assay vials (Total 1, Total 2, Initial 1, Initial 2) with 15‑second intervals, completing all additions within 1.5 min after centrifugation. Initial‑activity vials start the reaction immediately; total‑activity vials will receive RuBP after a 3‑minute incubation.

steps.title: Incubate and add RuBP for total activity
steps.instruction: Incubate the two total‑activity vials for 3 min at the assay temperature to allow Rubisco carbamylation. Then add 10 µL of 30 mM RuBP (Step 4) to each total‑activity vial.

steps.title: Quench reactions with formic acid
steps.instruction: Exactly 30 s after the start of each reaction (initial or total), quench by adding 100 µL of 10 M formic acid (Step 1.9).

steps.title: Prepare blanks and background checks
steps.instruction: For blanks, add 465 µL complete assay buffer (Step 8) plus 100 µL 10 M formic acid to each blank vial. For background checks, add 465 µL buffer and 25 µL extract, wait 3 min, then add 100 µL 10 M formic acid. Perform these at the start or end of the day.

steps.title: Verify radioactivity of assay buffer
steps.instruction: To test the radioactivity in the complete assay buffer, add 490 µL 0.3 M KOH (Step 1.8) and 10 µL of the complete assay buffer (Step 8) to a vial. Add 3.6 mL Gold Star Quanta scintillation cocktail (Step 1.10), close, and mix well. Dry the vial at 100 °C for ~1 h, then let cool. Add 400 µL ultrapure H₂O, wait 5 min, add another 3.6 mL scintillation cocktail, close, vortex, and count the ¹⁴C radioactivity with a scintillation counter.

steps.title: Count scintillation and calculate activity
steps.instruction: Measure ¹⁴C counts for each vial. Convert counts per minute (dpm) to µCi using 1 µCi = 2 220 000 dpm. Convert µCi to CO₂ concentration using the specific activity (0.5 Ci mol⁻¹). Calculate Rubisco activity per leaf area (µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹) or per protein (µmol CO₂ min⁻¹ mg⁻¹) by accounting for reaction time, extract volume, and sample leaf area or protein. Determine activation state (AS %) as 100 × Vᵢ / Vₜ, where Vᵢ is initial activity and Vₜ is total activity.
